column1: Default Sort Algorithm v3.1 — Public Specification
Source spec for github.com/reallyhq/default-sort. License: MIT.

Three-stage pipeline: Filter (Gate 1) → Tier (Gate 2 + Talk Now sub-tier + Gate 3) → Score (5 base factors × Reliability multiplier). Providers must have a completed Profile or Specialty page to appear in search results.

column5: Show provider pages in search results only if a bookable calendar slot exists in the next 14 days OR Talk Now toggle is currently active. No providers display unless this requirement is met.
Verified providers are always displayed above all Non-Verified providers. Within each Verified status, the Talk Now sub-tier applies (see below).

Within Verified bucket: Tier 1 = Verified + Talk Now active; Tier 2 = Verified + Calendar available (no Talk Now). Within Non-Verified bucket: Tier 3 = Not Verified + Talk Now active; Tier 4 = Not Verified + Calendar available (no Talk Now).

column1: BASE SCORE FACTORS (within-tier ranking; final_score = base_score × reliability_multiplier)

column6: Score 0-20. Continuous. Number of bookable calendar slots in the next 14 days. Higher availability earns more points up to maximum.
column7: Pulled from provider calendar. Dynamic and ongoing.

column6: Score 0-20. For Licensed: scaled by years in practice up to 20+ years. For Coaches: scaled by completed coaching hours up to 3,000+ hours. For Mentors: scaled by completed practice hours up to 2,000+ hours.
column7: Pulled from provider profile (Years in Practice / Completed Coaching Hours / Completed Practice Hours).

column6: Score 0-20. Continuous based on number and type of verified credentials held. More verified credentials earn more points up to maximum.
column7: Maps to verified licenses and certifications from provider profiles.

column6: Score 0-20. Bayesian formula: weighted_rating = (v / (v + m)) × R + (m / (v + m)) × C with m = 5. Points = max(0, (weighted_rating − 1) × 5).
column7: v = number of published reviews for the provider. R = provider mean rating. C = platform-wide mean rating recomputed nightly. Tech-only and removed reviews excluded from both R and C.

column6: Score 0 or 10 (binary). 10 points if Real-Time Audio Translation enabled on provider account (default-on at account creation); 0 points if provider has opted out. Awarded uniformly across all SERPs (population-multiplier capacity signal, not SERP-context signal).
column7: Pulled from provider account-level translation setting. Default-on at account creation; opting out costs 10 points relative to platform default.

column1: RELIABILITY SCORE MULTIPLIER (applied to base_score; final_score = base_score × multiplier)

column4: Highest reliability tier. Cold-start (<5 reliability events) defaults to Trusted.
Talk Now suspended (toggle forced off; provider remains visible via calendar path only). Multiplier persists 60 days after a 30-day Talk Now suspension lifts as recovery period.

column1: Reliability Score is computed from operational events (on-time pickup rate, late pickup rate, no-show rate, decline rate, session completion rate) over a rolling 30-day window. Cold-start providers (<5 events) default to Trusted (1.10×).

column2: Most recent profile update timestamp (DESC — more recently updated first)

column1: "Suspended" means Talk Now suspended NOT platform suspended
column2: A "Suspended" provider's Talk Now toggle is forced off and the Talk Now button is hidden from their profile. They continue to appear in search results via the calendar-availability path (Tier 2 or Tier 4) and their scheduled-session functionality is unaffected. Platform-level suspension is a separate Trust & Safety action and is NOT this algorithm.
Providers with fewer than 5 reliability events default to the Trusted multiplier (1.10×). The platform does not penalize new providers for absence of operational history.

After a 30-day Talk Now suspension is lifted, the provider's effective multiplier is held at 0.70× for 60 days as a recovery window, after which it reflects the then-current Reliability Score normally.
Default Sort returns the same order for every user. Personalization is post-MVP.
Cold-start handled neutrally via Bayesian shrinkage on Reviews and Trusted multiplier default. The platform does not apply favorable hidden boosts to new providers.

column1: Every factor in this algorithm is operational, not clinical. The platform observes facts (slot counts, credentials held, client speech in reviews, performance against operational commitments, capacity to serve cross-language sessions) and does NOT judge clinical care quality. The algorithm orders a directory; it does not practice medicine.

column2: Aggregating clinical screening tools into a sort signal moves the platform closer to making care-quality determinations. Deferred pending separate clinical and legal review.
Different from Real-Time Audio Translation Enablement (Factor 5), which is a population-multiplier capacity signal. Native fluency as a separate sort factor is pending dedicated review.

Whether Factor 5's 10 points should eventually be tied to actual translated session activity (rather than just the binary toggle state) is deferred. Decision informed by empirical data on opt-out rates and gaming behavior.
The 10-point value is provisional. Empirical data on ranking effects in mature locales may indicate the value should be retuned upward or downward.
An auto-off-style mechanism analogous to Talk Now's auto-off triggers, specific to translation-session quality (completion rate, client cancellation, latency thresholds), is post-MVP.
Default Sort returns the same order for every user. Personalization is post-MVP.

column1: This algorithm is published in full at https://github.com/reallyhq/default-sort under MIT license. Production code and the public spec are versioned together; any change to one requires a paired change to the other in the same release window. CI gates enforce that algorithm code changes require paired spec updates.

column3: Adds Real-Time Audio Translation Enablement as 5th base score factor (10 points binary, awarded uniformly across all SERPs). Base score range 0-80 → 0-90. Maximum effective score 88 → 99. The v3.0 three-stage architecture, four pre-v3.1 base score factors, Bayesian Reviews formula, Reliability multiplier, tier definitions, and Suspended-not-Platform-suspended distinction are preserved unchanged.

Initial public release. Three-stage architecture (Filter → Tier → Score). Four base score factors (Availability, Experience, Credentials, Bayesian-weighted Reviews). Reliability Score multiplier with cold-start handling. Supersedes unpublished v2.x drafts.
